newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's forint ends stronger vs dlr, NBH basket.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's forint ends stronger vs dlr, NBH basket.

text.p: Hungary's forint firmed against the dollar Tuesday afternoon, helped by the U.S. currency's losses on international markets and some forint purchases in a lacklustre market, dealers said.
"The dollar weakened against everything generally, and probably this encouraged (dollar) sellings," said ING Bank's Istvan Gere.
The forint finished at 175.85/90, up from 176.38/43 at midday and 176.50/55 at the opening.

The Hungarian unit also firmed against the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) currency basket, narrowing its gap from the NBH resistance level (bid) to about five pips at the end of the session from some 20 fillers earlier.
Dealers said trading was slow and the forint purchases which pushed the forint closer to the NBH bid were not very substantial.
The forint was also supported by a recent government decision to cut the monthly devaluation rate to 1.1 percent on April 1, from 1.2 percent, dealers added.

"Now that the devaluation rate has been reduced, it's worth again keeping short (foreign currency) positions," said Europai Kereskedelmi Bank's Andras Szanto. "If the forint went down, buyers would appear."
Dealers said the forint was likely to move in a range between five and 35 pips from the NBH bid in the near futures.
The forint floats in the NBH's 4.5 percent wide intervention band, against a basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
